title: feat(pm): fleet-write relay — closed op table, validator, executor, seat-side dispatcher, and the dispatch transport in the five write tools
body:
Part of #19701 — the seats' side of the fleet-write relay (PR B of two). The relay workflow itself is PR A, on `claude/issue-19701-fleet-write-relay`, which depends on this PR landing first. Nothing here needs PR A to be live: every tool keeps its `direct` transport, and `auto` falls back to it, out loud, when no relay run appears.

## What this adds

A cloud seat container cannot act as `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: its egress proxy replaces every `Authorization` header and refuses the `/app/**` mint path (the card's readings). What it can do is `POST /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/dispatches`. So a seat now packs the same requests it would have sent directly into ONE `repository_dispatch`, and the relay workflow (PR A) executes them as the fleet against the repository the payload names.

`scripts/pm/fleet-write/` — four files, one whitelist spelling:

- `ops.mjs` — the frozen op table: per op its required and optional keys, the endpoint(s) and verb it becomes, and the App permission it spends. The closed v1 list from the card: `comment`, `comment_edit`, `labels_add`, `labels_remove`, `assign`, `unassign`, `issue_patch` (title / body / state / state_reason only), `issue_create`, `pr_create` (`draft: true` forced), `pr_request_reviewers`, `pr_ready`, `pr_draft`, `automerge_enable` (`SQUASH`), `automerge_disable`. Merge, review submission, ref / contents / workflow writes, releases and org endpoints have no row, so the validator refuses them by construction, and its self-test pins that no request any op can spell reaches those families and none issues a whole-set `PUT`.
- `validate.mjs` — `validatePayload(obj) → { ok, errors, payload }`, hand-written, no dependency, imported by both the seat-side packer and the runner. Closed envelope `{ request_id ≤ 64, repo: objectstack-ai/NAME, session: session_…, actions: 1..20 }`; unknown top-level or per-action keys refused by name; integers must be JSON numbers; strings capped in bytes (body ≤ 60000, title ≤ 256, label ≤ 50); lists capped and de-duplicated; enums closed. The platform's own `client_payload` ceilings are pinned with their source: at most 10 top-level properties and under 64KB (GitHub's REST OpenAPI description for "Create a repository dispatch event"). `--from-env --github-output` is the runner's spelling; a refusal writes every reason to the step summary with zero writes.
- `execute.mjs` — the runner-side executor. Sender gate first: `GET /repos/{payload.repo}/collaborators/{sender}/permission`, allowed only for `write` / `maintain` / `admin` (GitHub folds `maintain` into `permission: write`; `role_name` is read too), a 404 or a lesser role is a run failure with zero writes. Then the actions in order, stop at the first failure (later actions not attempted, and the summary says so); a 404 on a directed label DELETE is idempotent success; the GraphQL ops read the pull's node id first and treat an `errors` array as failure. Every write is paced through `write-pace.mjs`. The step summary table: request id · sender and role · session · target · one row per request (op, endpoint, HTTP status, id / url). The token arrives only through `GITHUB_TOKEN`, is never printed or written, and every emitted line is scrubbed — the self-test feeds a known token through a platform that echoes it and greps every output.
- `dispatch.mjs` — the seat side. `OS_FLEET_TRANSPORT ∈ direct | dispatch | auto` (default `auto`). `auto` is `dispatch` only when ALL THREE hold: ① `CCR_AGENT_PROXY_ENABLED=1` (the variable naming the proxy whose header replacement is the reason; never the proxy port), ② a well-formed `OS_FLEET_SESSION=session_…` on the envelope, ③ the relay live on the board — `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/contents/.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml?ref=main` answering 200, read once per process and cached, and only reached once ① and ② hold. Any condition failing ⇒ `direct`, with one printed line naming it and no start-window wait: a seat that has not opted in, or a board without the listening workflow, keeps today's behaviour at today's speed. An explicit `OS_FLEET_TRANSPORT=dispatch` stays strict — a missing session or a relay that is not live is a prerequisite refusal (exit 3), never a fall-back. Once `dispatch` is taken: one paced dispatch per stroke, then the run-poller (`display_title` carrying the request id, then the run until `completed`); the two ceilings `OS_FLEET_DISPATCH_START_MS` (90 s) and `OS_FLEET_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 min) answer `UNCONFIRMED` (exit 6) with the run URL, never retried, and under `auto` a live-but-silent relay (no run in the start window) falls back to `direct` with one line naming the double-write risk. `with-fleet.sh --via auto` asks the same selector (`dispatch.mjs --route`). `OS_FLEET_RELAY_LIVE=1|0` overrides ③ for tests only and says so.

The five write tools take the transport, each keeping its shape:

- `label-write.mjs` — steps ①, ② and ④ unchanged; step ③ packs the adds, the directed removes and the assignee change of this one write into one dispatch (`relayActions`, the same verbs in the same order as the direct plan). The whole-set `PATCH` fallback stays `direct`-only: the relay has additive verbs only. An idempotent no-op dispatches nothing.
- `post-stamped.mjs` — the stamp is substituted before packing (the stamp is the seat's act); one `comment` or one `issue_patch { body }`; afterwards the stored body is read from the board (the newest comment since the dispatch whose stored body is the one sent, footer-appending and newline-stripping counted as landed) and judged by the same `readBackVerdict` as the direct path. Exit register kept apart: a refused dispatch is 3 (no act), a failed run is 4 (go read), no run or no completion is 6.
- `issue-create.mjs` — one `issue_create`; the new number is found by title among issues created since the dispatch, then the ordinary read-back.
- `close-cards.mjs` — the comment goes through `post-stamped` as before (the child resolves its own transport from the same environment), the label write is handed this run's route, the close is one `issue_patch { state: closed, state_reason }` read back from the card. A relay miss on the close is a half-write: the run stops there naming the run.
- `with-fleet.sh` — `--via direct | dispatch | auto` (or `OS_FLEET_TRANSPORT`). `--via dispatch --repo owner/name --actions actions.json` sends an actions file through the relay (the door for ops no node tool owns: `pr_ready`, `automerge_enable`, reviewers…); a command after `--` under `auto` in a cloud container is refused (exit 3) with that spelling, because the identity cannot be minted there and running it as the session login instead would be a silent change of identity. An explicit `--via direct` still wins.

`write-pace.mjs`: the roster of write-verb files gains the two relay halves (its own self-test demanded it — a write verb in `scripts/pm` must be on the roster and call both halves), and the roster is now spelled repo-relative (`scripts/pm/…`). Reason, measured: `check:pm-dispatch-gates` reads every separator-bearing literal in a gate's source as a path lead; a bare `fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` resolved to nothing from the repo root, printed as a dead lead under the write-pace family, and its live self-test battery miscounted that row (1 of 1906 cases red, reproduced without contention). Repo-relative entries are live leads, so a card touching any roster file now names the write-pace gate — the right answer, since that self-test reads those files. The roster's consumers were respelled to match, which is the one line this PR touches in `fleet-token.mjs` (outside the card's file surface; mechanical, same gate family). The same derivation then listed the three new gate families as unreachable (their only separator-bearing literals at module scope named no tracked path), so `ops.mjs` declares `RELAY_FILES` — the relay's four files, repo-relative, checked on disk by the validator's self-test — which gives each family a live lead through the import channel; on a tree carrying both PRs the derivation reports 0 unreachable families. `package.json`: `check:pm-fleet-write-validate`, `check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`, spelled like `check:pm-post-stamped`; the `lint.yml` steps that run them are in PR A (a workflow file).

## The permissions the relay token needs (for PR A's mint)

From GitHub's server-to-server permission ledger (`github/docs`, `src/github-apps/data/fpt-2022-11-28/server-to-server-permissions.json`, read 2026-09-22, docs.github.com itself being unreachable from this container): every `/issues/**` write here is `issues: write`; `POST /pulls`, `POST /pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers` and the pull-request mutations are `pull-requests: write`; `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{login}/permission` is `metadata: read`. `PERMISSIONS` in `ops.mjs` is exactly that set and PR A declares exactly it on `actions/create-github-app-token@v2` (`permission-issues`, `permission-pull-requests`, `permission-metadata`). Not measured: whether `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` needs `contents: write` in addition — the live probe decides it; the fix would be one more `permission-contents: write` line in PR A, deliberately not pre-granted.

## Verification

Every self-test offline, no network, run from the pushed tree (`git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `b656a69`):

```
node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test   → 69 cases, 7 batteries
node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs  --self-test   → 48 cases, 9 batteries
node scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --self-test   → 48 cases, 8 batteries
node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs          --self-test   → 88 cases, 10 batteries (+12 relay)
node scripts/pm/issue-create.mjs         --self-test   → 42 cases, 6 batteries (+8 relay)
node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs         --self-test   → 574 cases, 20 batteries (+12 relay)
node scripts/pm/close-cards.mjs          --self-test   → 111 cases, 12 batteries (+8 relay)
bash scripts/pm/with-fleet.sh            --self-test   → 30 cases (+10 --via)
node scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs           --self-test   → 109 cases, 12 batteries (the nine-file roster)
node scripts/pm/fleet-token.mjs          --self-test   → 73 cases, 8 batteries (the respelled roster row)
```

Derived gate families (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, no paths, off the merge base): 43 families reconciled with `--ran` at `b656a69` — 39 run green, 4 NOT MEASURED (each exits 3 because it loads built `dist/`, which this diff never touches and CI builds: `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`), 0 unrun. `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (run separately, ~15 min on this box): 1906/1906 cases on this head, and 1906/1906 on a throwaway tree carrying this head plus PR A's two workflow files, where the derivation also reports 0 unreachable families and `check-self-test-wired` (production and `--self-test`), `check-self-test-workflow-commands`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:workflow-step-name-quoting` and `check-step-collectors` are green.

`pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the nine changed / new files: clean.

Not measured here, by design: the live dispatch. A dispatch to the board without the listening workflow answers 204 and no run (the card's reading); exercising that path costs a write outside this run's budget, so the start-window and completion ceilings are defaults, to be tuned from the first live probe after PR A lands.

## Acceptance notes

- `close-cards` under `dispatch` spends up to three relay runs per card (comment, label, close). Folding the three into one payload would be faster and keeps the executor's stop-at-first-failure order, but it would move the stamp rendering and the label arithmetic out of the tools that own them; left as three strokes. Carrier: none.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` and `label-write.mjs` import each other (`classifyHttp` one way, the transport the other). Both use the imported bindings only inside functions, so the ESM cycle is inert; noted for the next reader.
- `with-fleet.sh --read` under `auto` in a cloud container is refused like a write: the wrapper's whole job is the fleet identity, which cannot be minted there; a read that needs no identity does not need the wrapper.
- The seat-side references (`rest-channel.md`, `platform-readings.md`) do not yet describe `OS_FLEET_TRANSPORT` / `OS_FLEET_SESSION`; the card leaves documentation to the seat's own card.
